locus: Theses in quibus exponitur Doctrina Scholae Romanae circa partitionem Gratiae in sufficientem atque efficacem, & concordiam libertatis humanae cum Gratiae efficacia, CXLI-CXLV, end of locus (appendix on Gregory of Valencia SJ: efficacious grace as a gift obtainable by devout use of free choice, prior to conversion as efficient cause and posterior as material and dispositive cause; the gift is the infusion of habits of grace and the virtues; his account of sufficient grace (tome 2, disp. 8, q. 3, punct. 4); he sides with the recent Thomists against Molina and the congruists on a new aid, but with the later theologians on efficacy depending on free choice; Le Blanc's two objections). The Roman locus ends with CXLV at the foot of its text on book 542, followed by the title of the Protestant locus.
next_locus: Theses in quibus exponitur Doctrina Protestantium circa distinctionem Gratiae in sufficientem atque efficacem, & concordiam libertatis humanae cum efficacia gratiae divinae, Thesis I onward (new locus: the Lutherans of the Augsburg Confession; PDF 558-, book 542-)
